column4: Visit note | 2026-06-01 10:30 AM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Abdul Mollah, 75, male. Mr. Mollah states he experiences brief spinning when turning in bed, dizziness when looking up, and nausea with the spinning. He mentions the trouble began after a viral cold in Old Dhaka. He is a retired civil servant and lives with his family. He reports no hearing loss or ringing in his ears. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the left side, BP 110/74 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 58 kg. Cranial nerves are intact. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2026-06-02 10:00 AM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Farzana Chowdhury, 75, female. Mrs. Chowdhury returns for review and reports she experiences spinning only when lying on one side, with no nausea, brief spinning when turning in bed, and dizziness when looking up. She notes this started after bumping the head on a rickshaw hood in Gazipur. She is a homemaker and has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She takes her diabetes medications regularly and has no focal weakness. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the right side, BP 125/83 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 49 kg. Gait is steady with support. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
